Why the future of the planet will be coded, not just conserved

A Q U E S T I O N B E F O R E W E S T A R T
Why should a computer science student
sit through a lecture on sustainability?
Because climate technology is quietly becoming one of the fastest-growing, most 
talent-starved segments of the entire tech industry — and almost nobody in this 
room is positioned for it yet.
That gap is your opening.
3×

software roles (illustrative trend)
<2%
Of engineering graduates currently target climate-tech 
careers — meaning far less competition for you
SUST AI N AB I LI T Y & CLI MAT E CH AN GE 02

Your CSE syllabus is already a climate-tech syllabus
Every core subject you have already studied — or are studying right now — has a direct climate application.
Data Structures & Algorithms Optimizing energy routing and real-time grid load balancing
Machine Learning Climate forecasting, weather prediction, emissions modeling
Database Systems ESG reporting and enterprise carbon-accounting platforms
Computer Networks / IoT Smart grids, precision agriculture, environmental sensor networks
Cloud Computing Planetary-scale climate simulation and renewable-asset coordination
Cybersecurity Protecting power grids and critical climate infrastructure
04

B E F O R E W E B E G I N
You are not in the wrong major.
For fifteen years, sustainability has been taught as an environmental science 
elective — soil, carbon cycles, ecosystems. That story is now incomplete.
The next chapter of climate action is being written in code — in models, sensors, 
algorithms and systems. That is your language.
The old assumption
"Sustainability = Environmental Science."
A subject for biologists, not engineers.
The new reality
AI, IoT, robotics and software now decide 
whether climate solutions actually scale.

T H E P R O P O S E D M A T R I X
Nine Technologies, Mapped to Nine Problems
Before the deep dives: the framework connecting each technology to the specific climate problem it solves, and the shift in approach it represents.
T E C H N O L O G Y T H E E X I S T I N G P R O B L E M T H E P R O P O S E D S H I F T
AI & Machine Learning Slow, compute-heavy prediction Learned models — seconds, not hours
Data Science & Analytics Manual, annual, error-prone reporting Automated, continuous pipelines
Internet of Things Sparse, infrequent physical-world data Real-time sensor networks

N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 11

01
AI & Machine
Learning
The predictive brain of the climate system —
forecasting, optimizing, and discovering faster 
than any human team.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Traditional weather and climate prediction solves physics equations on supercomputers — accurate, 
but slow (hours per forecast) and accessible only to a handful of national agencies.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Learn patterns instead of solving equations
Train models directly on decades of historical atmospheric data so they learn the patterns physics simulations 
compute from scratch every time.
Forecast in seconds, not hours
A trained model can generate a 10-day global forecast in under a minute, on a single machine — no 
supercomputer queue required.
Extend the same approach beyond weather
The same learned-pattern approach now optimizes energy grids and predicts emissions and financial risk.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 12

01
AI & Machine
Learning
-40%
Reduction in data center cooling energy after DeepMind 
applied the same ML approach to Google's own cooling 
systems.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Google DeepMind — GraphCast
A graph neural network trained on 40 years of reanalysis weather data. It predicts 10-day global weather in under a 
minute, outperforming the world's leading physics-based model (ECMWF's HRES) on the majority of tested variables.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Physics-based Numerical Weather Prediction: hours of 
dedicated supercomputer time per forecast, run by a 
handful of national meteorological agencies 
worldwide.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
ML-based forecasting: under 60 seconds on a single 
TPU/GPU, in principle deployable by any team with 
access to training data.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
The field of "AI for weather and climate" barely existed five years ago. A genuinely novel model architecture is still a 
realistic student research project today — not a solved problem you'd be repeating.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 13

02
Data Science &
Analytics
Turning billions of scattered climate signals into 
decisions leaders can act on.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Corporate and national emissions reporting has long relied on annual, manually compiled, self￾reported estimates — slow, inconsistent, and easy to get wrong or game.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Automate the data pipeline
Continuously ingest utility bills, IoT sensor feeds, and supply-chain data instead of collecting it once a year by 
hand.
Calculate emissions near real time
Turn a process that once took months into a dashboard that updates automatically as new data arrives.
Flag anomalies automatically
Statistical and ML models catch reporting errors and undisclosed emissions spikes that manual review would 
miss.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 14

02
Data Science &
Analytics
2.5 Qt
Bytes of Earth-observation and sensor data now generated 
daily that platforms like this increasingly draw on.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Watershed
A carbon accounting SaaS platform used by companies including Airbnb and Block to automate what used to be a 
multi-month manual audit into a continuously updated emissions dashboard.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Annual manual spreadsheet audits, often outsourced 
to consultants, published 6–12 months after the 
reporting period already ended.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Continuous, API-driven emissions dashboards that 
update automatically as new operational data arrives.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
Every company on Earth will eventually need a pipeline like this. The market for it is still being built, not yet 
saturated — early movers are defining the category.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 15

03
Internet of
Things (IoT)
Millions of low-cost sensors turning the physical 
world into a real-time climate dashboard.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Utilities and farmers have traditionally operated on sparse data — a monthly meter reading, a manual 
soil check — making it impossible to catch problems like leaks or drought stress until well after they 
start.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Deploy dense, continuous sensor networks
Low-cost sensors stream data constantly instead of being checked on a calendar schedule.
Enable automated, real-time response
Systems can trigger demand-response signals or precision irrigation the moment conditions change — not 
weeks later.
Push decisions to the edge
Many IoT climate systems now process data locally, reacting in milliseconds without waiting on a round trip to 
the cloud.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 16

03
Internet of
Things (IoT)
29 Bn
IoT-connected devices projected worldwide by 2030 — a 
huge share feeding climate and energy systems.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
CropX
A soil-sensor IoT network used by farmers worldwide to cut water use significantly while improving yields, by 
irrigating only where and when the underlying soil data actually calls for it.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Monthly manual meter readings; calendar-based (not 
data-based) irrigation scheduling regardless of actual 
soil conditions.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Real-time sensor networks driving automated, minute￾by-minute irrigation and consumption decisions.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
IoT-for-climate is as much a hardware, firmware, and networking problem as a software one — there is room here 
for nearly every CSE specialization.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 17

04
Digital Twins
Living, simulated replicas of cities, grids and 
factories — where climate strategies are tested 
before they cost a rupee.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Cities and industrial facilities have historically been designed and built first — only discovering 
flooding, overheating, or energy-inefficiency problems afterward, when fixing them is disruptive and 
expensive.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Build a high-fidelity virtual replica first
Model the physical system in enough detail to simulate real climate stresses against it.
Simulate before construction, not after
Test heatwaves, flooding, and energy loads virtually, catching flaws while they still cost nothing to fix.
Keep the twin live post-construction
Twins continue tracking the real asset afterward, predicting maintenance needs and failure points.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 18

04
Digital Twins
$13 Bn
Projected market for industrial digital twins, growing fastest 
in energy and infrastructure sectors.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Virtual Singapore
A detailed 3D digital twin of the entire city-state, used by planners to simulate heatwave impact, flooding, and solar 
potential before greenlighting real infrastructure spending.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Build first, retrofit later — trial-and-error in the 
physical world, at a cost measured in disrupted cities 
and wasted concrete.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Simulate extensively in the virtual world first; only 
build what has already been stress-tested against 
climate scenarios.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
Every digital twin is, at its core, a distributed-simulation and data-engineering problem — a natural fit if you enjoy 
systems, graphics, or large-scale modeling.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 19

05
Robotics &
Automation
Machines doing the dull, dangerous and large￾scale climate work humans physically cannot.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Reforestation and ocean cleanup have long depended on human labor — slow, expensive, and 
capped at a tiny fraction of the scale actually needed, versus the millions of hectares and tons 
involved.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Automate what humans can't scale
Deploy drones, autonomous vessels, and vision-guided robots to work at industrial scale, not volunteer-crew 
scale.
Operate in conditions humans can't sustain
Robots work continuously in heat, remote terrain, or open ocean without shift limits or safety exposure.
Run around the clock
Unlike human crews, autonomous systems don't stop for weather, daylight, or rest.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 20

05
Robotics &
Automation
24/7
Operating capability of autonomous cleanup and sorting 
systems — work that never stops for weather or shifts.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
The Ocean Cleanup
Autonomous vessel systems that have removed millions of kilograms of plastic from the Pacific Ocean, operating 
continuously without needing a full-time onboard crew.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Small human crews, limited by weather, safety, and 
cost, realistically able to cover only a tiny fraction of 
the affected area.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Autonomous systems operating around the clock, at a 
small fraction of the marginal cost per hectare or 
kilogram removed.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
Climate robotics is still mostly unsolved outside a few flagship projects — huge open problems remain in perception, 
navigation, and long-term durability.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 21

06
Cloud
Computing
The planetary-scale compute layer that makes 
climate modeling and coordination even 
possible.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Until recently, running a serious climate model required an allocation on one of a handful of national 
supercomputing centers — a queue of weeks to months, inaccessible to most researchers, let alone 
students or startups.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Rent compute instead of queuing for it
Provision massive, elastic capacity by the hour from commercial cloud providers.
Run the same class of simulation, for less
Ensemble climate models that once needed a supercomputing grant now run on rented cloud HPC clusters.
Coordinate distributed assets, not just compute
Cloud platforms also coordinate thousands of rooftop solar and battery assets as a single "virtual power plant."
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 22

06
Cloud
Computing
1000s
Of virtual servers spun up in minutes to run climate 
ensembles that once took months to schedule.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Cloud-based climate ensembles
Climate researchers and startups increasingly run large ensemble simulations on commercial cloud HPC clusters, 
spinning up thousands of virtual servers in minutes for workloads that once required a supercomputing allocation.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Apply for time on a national supercomputer; wait 
weeks to months for an allocation; share capacity with 
every other funded project.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Provision cloud HPC capacity on demand, pay only for 
what is used, and scale down the moment the run 
finishes.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
You can now run a genuinely serious climate simulation from a laptop and a credit card. The barrier to entry that 
once required an institutional affiliation has essentially collapsed.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 23

07
Cybersecurity
Protecting the grids, dams and sensor networks 
that a decarbonized world will depend on 
completely.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Power grids, water treatment plants, and renewable assets were designed assuming they'd never 
touch the internet — "security by obscurity." As they digitize for efficiency, that assumption has 
quietly become false, with almost no built-in defense.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Monitor OT, not just IT
Purpose-built operational technology (OT) security watches industrial control traffic for anomalies specific to 
energy infrastructure.
Assume connectivity, not obscurity
Design defenses for grids that are — and will remain — network-connected, rather than pretending they are 
air-gapped.
Protect data integrity, not just uptime
Verifying that emissions and climate data hasn't been tampered with is now its own security discipline.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 24

07
Cybersecurity
+150%
Rise in reported cyberattacks on energy infrastructure over 
the past few years as grids digitize.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Dragos
An industrial cybersecurity company focused specifically on protecting power grids, water systems, and 
manufacturing plants from cyberattacks, used by utilities across North America and Europe.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Generic IT security tooling — or often no monitoring at 
all — on systems assumed to be "air-gapped" and 
therefore unreachable.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
OT-specific threat detection purpose-built for the 
unique protocols and failure modes of energy 
infrastructure.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
This is one of the most under-supplied specializations in all of cybersecurity — most security engineers today have 
never touched an industrial control system.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 25

08
Blockchain
A transparent, tamper-proof ledger for a carbon 
economy that has long struggled with trust.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
Voluntary carbon credit markets have long been plagued by double-counting, opaque registries, and 
outright fraud — buyers often cannot verify that the reduction they paid for is real, or hasn't already 
been sold to someone else.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Record credits on a shared, tamper-evident ledger
Every credit's origin and full ownership history becomes independently verifiable by anyone.
Cut out the middleman where it adds no value
Peer-to-peer platforms let households trade surplus solar power directly, without a utility intermediary.
Extend traceability up the supply chain
The same ledger approach verifies the origin of "green" materials, from cobalt to sustainable timber.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 26

08
Blockchain
$2 Bn+
Value flowing through blockchain-based carbon-market and 
renewable-trading platforms today.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Power Ledger
A blockchain-based platform enabling households with rooftop solar to trade surplus energy directly with neighbors, 
without a utility as middleman — deployed in Australia, Japan, Thailand, and beyond.
O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Centralized, often opaque registries prone to double￾counting; utility-mediated energy trading with no peer￾to-peer option.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Transparent, cryptographically verifiable ledgers 
enabling direct, trustless peer-to-peer trading.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
Trust infrastructure for climate markets is still being invented — this is genuinely greenfield territory, even within an 
otherwise mature blockchain field.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 27

09
Software
Engineering
The invisible discipline that turns every idea 
above from a prototype into something that 
actually ships and scales.
P AR T 1 O F 2 · P R O B L EM & S O L U TIO N
T H E P R O B L E M
For decades, climate and environmental datasets sat locked inside individual institutions —
incompatible formats, no shared APIs — forcing every new project to rebuild the same data pipeline 
from scratch.
T H E P R O P O S E D S O L U T I O N
Engineer for sharing, not just for use
Build well-documented public APIs instead of one-off internal data formats.
Let an ecosystem build on shared infrastructure
Thousands of independent developers can innovate on the same underlying data instead of duplicating 
collection effort.
Bring engineering rigor to every idea on this list
Every model, sensor network, and trading platform in this lecture is only as reliable as the software holding it 
together.
N I N E T E CH N OLOGIE S · CLI MAT E ACT I ON 28

09
Software
Engineering
1
Discipline every technology on this list depends on to go 
from lab demo to planetary-scale deployment: yours.
P AR T 2 O F 2 · C AS E S TU DY & C O M P AR IS O N
C A S E S T U D Y
Climate TRACE
A coalition combining AI and satellite data that built an open API tracking greenhouse gas emissions from over 660 
million individual sources worldwide — letting any developer build on top of it instead of gathering the data

O L D M O D E L v s . N E W M O D E L
THE EXISTING MODEL
Bespoke, closed data silos — every team re-solves the 
same integration problem before any real climate work 
can begin.
THE PROPOSED MODEL
Shared, well-engineered open APIs (Climate TRACE, 
NASA) that an entire ecosystem of builders works on 
top of.
W H Y T H I S S H O U L D E X C I T E Y O U
This is the least glamorous and most essential technology on the list — and the one almost every other climate-tech 
job actually needs on a daily basis.

S E C T I O N 1 · T H E R A T E P R O B L E M
A Planet That Has Never Changed This Fast
Earth's climate has always changed — but the speed of the current change is what makes it unprecedented.
Natural Change Is Slow Past ice ages and warm periods unfolded over thousands to tens of thousands of years, giving ecosystems time 
to adapt or migrate.
This Change Is Fast The current pace of warming is estimated to be at least 10 times faster than the fastest natural warming after 
the last ice age.
Why Speed Matters Evolution, migration, and human adaptation all take time. A planet that changes in decades, not millennia, 
leaves little room to adjust.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · I N T R ODUCT I ON T O CLI MAT E CH AN GE 08

S E C T I O N 2 O F 6
What Do We Mean by "Climate 
Change"?
A term used constantly in the news — and defined precisely, and specifically, in science.
09

S E C T I O N 2 · G E T T I N G P R E C I S E
What Is Climate Change, Exactly?
The IPCC and the UNFCCC define it slightly differently — and the difference matters.
IPCC Definition Any change in the state of the climate, identifiable by changes in its mean and/or variability, persisting for 
decades or longer — regardless of cause.
UNFCCC Definition A change in climate attributed directly or indirectly to human activity, altering atmospheric composition, in 
addition to natural variability.
Why It Matters The UNFCCC's narrower, human-caused definition is the one used in international climate policy, law, and 
negotiation — including everything in Units ahead.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · I N T R ODUCT I ON T O CLI MAT E CH AN GE 10

S E C T I O N 2 · A Q U I C K D I S T I N C T I O N
Weather vs. Climate — In Brief
Weather Climate
What the atmosphere is doing right now, in one place. The long-term pattern and average of weather, over decades.
Changes hour to hour, day to day. Changes gradually, over decades to centuries.
"It is unusually hot in Delhi today." "Delhi's climate is getting hotter, decade over decade."
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · I N T R ODUCT I ON T O CLI MAT E CH AN GE 11

◆ INTERACTIVE Q U I C K C H E C K
Myth or Fact?
MYTH "Climate change" and "global warming" mean exactly the same 
thing.
Global warming is one symptom (rising temperature). Climate change is the broader 
phenomenon — also including shifting rainfall, extreme weather, and sea level rise.
MYTH A single freezing week in Delhi disproves global warming.
One region's short-term weather event says nothing about a decades-long global 
average trend — this is one of the most common reasoning errors in the public 
debate.
MYTH Scientists are still genuinely divided on whether this is happening.
Over 97% of actively publishing climate scientists agree recent warming is real and 
predominantly human-caused — the debate in the literature is about impact and 
response, not existence.
FACT Earth's climate has changed naturally before, many times. True — ice ages and warm periods are part of Earth's history. What is different now is 
the rate of change and the clearly identified human cause.

Six Ways We Measure a Changing Climate
Different tools, different teams, different decades — and they all tell the same story.
Direct Thermometers
Global surface temperature records dating back to the 1880s, 
from thousands of stations worldwide.
Ice Cores
Ancient air bubbles trapped in Antarctic and Greenland ice reveal 
atmospheric CO₂ going back 800,000 years.
Satellites
Since 1979, satellites have independently measured 
temperature, sea level, and ice extent from orbit.

Photographed and measured glacier boundaries worldwide show 
consistent, accelerating retreat.

Tide gauges and satellite altimetry both confirm accelerating sea 
level rise since the early 20th century.
Tree Rings & Corals
Natural growth records extend the climate record thousands of 
years before instruments existed.

S E C T I O N 1 · T H E F I V E S P H E R E S
The Components of Earth's Climate System
Climate emerges from constant interaction between five great subsystems of the planet.
Atmosphere
The blanket of gases 
surrounding Earth — where 
weather happens and 
greenhouse gases trap heat.
Hydrosphere
All of Earth's water — oceans, 
lakes, rivers, and groundwater 
— which stores and transports 
vast amounts of heat.
Cryosphere
Frozen water — ice sheets, 
glaciers, sea ice, and 
permafrost — which reflects 
sunlight and locks away 
carbon.
Lithosphere
Earth's solid crust and upper 
mantle, including soil and rock, 
which slowly cycles carbon 
over geological time.
Biosphere
All living organisms — plants, 
animals, and microbes — that 
absorb and release carbon 
through life processes.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · T H E SCI E N CE E N GI N E OF CLI MAT E CH AN GE 06

S E C T I O N 1 · E N E R G Y B A L A N C E
Earth's Energy Balance
For Earth's temperature to stay stable, incoming solar energy must roughly equal outgoing energy. Climate change disrupts this balance.
SUN
Incoming solar radiation (100 units)
EARTH
Greenhouse gas layer — intercepts part of the outgoing heat
~30 units reflected back to space by clouds, ice & 
bright surfaces (albedo)
~70 units absorbed & re-emitted as heat (long￾wave radiation)
W H Y T H E B A L A N C E M A T T E R S
Roughly 30% of incoming solar energy is reflected straight back to space 
by clouds, ice, and bright surfaces (this is called albedo).
The remaining ~70% is absorbed by Earth and re-radiated as heat (long￾wave/infrared radiation).
Greenhouse gases absorb some of that outgoing heat and re-emit it back 
down — this is the natural greenhouse effect.
More greenhouse gases means more heat trapped, and the balance 
point shifts to a warmer Earth.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · T H E SCI E N CE E N GI N E OF CLI MAT E CH AN GE 07

S E C T I O N 1 · A S Y S T E M S V I E W
Climate as Earth's Largest Distributed System
As computer scientists, you already have the mental model for this — you just haven't applied it here yet.
Nodes & State The five spheres are like distributed nodes, each holding and exchanging state (heat, carbon, water) with the 
others.
Feedback Loops Melting ice reduces reflectivity, which increases absorbed heat, which melts more ice — a positive feedback 
loop, exactly like a runaway process in a control system.
Latency & Buffering The ocean acts as a massive buffer, absorbing and slowly releasing heat over years to decades — much like a 
cache with very high latency.
Why It's Hard Like any large distributed system, small local changes can propagate into large global effects — making the 
system genuinely difficult to predict precisely.

The Greenhouse Effect
The natural process that makes life possible — and the mechanism behind global warming when amplified.

S E C T I O N 2 · T H E P R O C E S S W E N E E D
The Greenhouse Effect Keeps Us Alive
Without any greenhouse effect at all, Earth would be a frozen, uninhabitable rock.
Without It Earth's average temperature would be roughly -18°C — about 33°C colder than it is today. Oceans would freeze.
With the Natural Effect Greenhouse gases trap just enough heat to keep Earth's average temperature around a life-friendly +15°C.
The Problem Isn't the Effect Itself The problem is that human emissions have intensified this natural process well beyond its historical equilibrium 
— an enhanced, human-amplified greenhouse effect.

1. Sunlight arrives

S E C T I O N 2 · K E Y P L A Y E R S
Major Greenhouse Gases & Their Sources
Not all greenhouse gases are equal — they differ hugely in abundance, lifetime, and heat-trapping strength.
Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)
Fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, cement production. ~76% of human GHG emissions by volume — the 
primary driver due to sheer quantity.
Methane (CH₄)
Livestock digestion, rice paddies, landfills, natural gas leaks. Traps far more heat per molecule than CO₂, but 
breaks down faster (~12 years).
Nitrous Oxide (N₂O) Synthetic fertilizers, industrial processes. Roughly 265–298 times more warming per molecule than CO₂ over a 
100-year period.
Water Vapour & F-gases
Water vapour is the largest natural greenhouse gas but responds to warming rather than driving it; F-gases (from 
refrigerants, industry) are synthetic and extremely potent.

What Is Driving Global Warming?

Factors
Solar cycles — minor fluctuations in the sun's output over ~11-year cycles. Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) for energy, industry, and transport.

S E C T I O N 3 · W H Y E N G I N E E R S S H O U L D C A R E
Feedback Loops & Tipping Points
This is where your background in systems and nonlinear dynamics becomes directly useful.
Positive Feedback: Ice-Albedo Less ice → less sunlight reflected → more heat absorbed → more ice melts. A self-reinforcing loop, just like 
unstable positive feedback in a control system.
Positive Feedback: Permafrost Carbon Warming thaws permafrost → releases trapped methane and CO₂ → causes more warming → thaws more 
permafrost.
Tipping Points Beyond certain thresholds, these feedback loops can become self-sustaining even if human emissions stopped 
— the climate equivalent of a system that has left its stable operating region.
Why This Matters for Prediction Nonlinear systems with feedback loops are notoriously hard to forecast precisely — which is exactly why climate 
models require immense computational power.

S E C T I O N 4 · T H E S Y S T E M
The Carbon Cycle
Carbon continuously flows between four great reservoirs. Under natural conditions, what leaves one enters another in balance.
Atmosphere
~875 GtC
Ocean
~38,000 GtC
Land / Biosphere
~2,000 GtC
Fossil Fuels & Rock
~10,000,000 GtC
K E Y F L U X E S B E T W E E N R E S E R V O I R S
Photosynthesis
Plants absorb atmospheric CO₂ to build biomass (Atmosphere → Biosphere).
Respiration & Decay
Organisms release CO₂ back to the atmosphere as they breathe and decompose.
Ocean Exchange
Oceans absorb and release CO₂ at the surface; the ocean is currently a net carbon sink.
Combustion (Human)
Burning fossil fuels releases carbon locked away for millions of years — the cycle's 
biggest disruption.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · T H E SCI E N CE E N GI N E OF CLI MAT E CH AN GE 25

S E C T I O N 4 · T W O S P E E D S
The Fast Cycle vs. the Slow Cycle
Fast Carbon Cycle Slow Carbon Cycle
Moves carbon between atmosphere, ocean surface, and living things. Moves carbon between rocks, sediments, and the deep ocean.
Timescale: days to centuries. Timescale: thousands to millions of years.
Example: a tree absorbing CO₂ through photosynthesis. Example: carbon slowly locked into limestone or fossil fuel deposits.
This is the cycle humans have dramatically disrupted. Fossil fuel combustion pulls slow-cycle carbon into the fast cycle — the core of 
the problem.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · T H E SCI E N CE E N GI N E OF CLI MAT E CH AN GE 26

S E C T I O N 4 · H U M A N D I S R U P T I O N
How Humans Have Unbalanced the Carbon Cycle
The carbon cycle balanced itself for millennia. Two human activities changed that.
Fossil Fuel Combustion Releases carbon that took millions of years to accumulate underground, on a timescale of decades — far faster 
than natural sinks can reabsorb it.
Deforestation & Land-Use Change Destroys biosphere carbon sinks and releases stored carbon, while also reducing Earth's future capacity to 
absorb CO₂.
Net Result Atmospheric CO₂ has risen from ~280 ppm (pre-industrial) to over 420 ppm today — the highest level in at least 
800,000 years.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · T H E SCI E N CE E N GI N E OF CLI MAT E CH AN GE 27

S E C T I O N 4 · A N E N G I N E E R ' S F R A M I N G
The Global Carbon Budget Is a Ledger Problem
Think of it as an accounting system running a structural deficit.
The Budget Concept Scientists estimate a finite "carbon budget" — the total CO₂ humanity can still emit while keeping warming 
under 1.5°C or 2°C.
Withdrawals vs. Deposits Fossil fuel combustion is a withdrawal; reforestation and carbon capture are deposits. Right now, withdrawals 
vastly outpace deposits.
Why This Resonates With CS It is fundamentally a resource-accounting and optimization problem — tracking flows, sources, and sinks at 
planetary scale, which is exactly the kind of system engineers are trained to model and manage.
CLI MAT E & SUST AI N AB I LI T Y · T H E SCI E N CE E N GI N E OF CLI MAT E CH AN GE 28

Which of these best describes why fossil fuel combustion is so 
disruptive to the carbon cycle?
A It creates a new type of carbon molecule never seen before

It moves slow-cycle carbon into the fast cycle far faster than natural processes can absorb

A N S W E R & W H Y
B. It moves slow-cycle carbon into the fast 
cycle far faster than natural processes can

Fossil fuels represent carbon that was locked away in 
the slow cycle over millions of years. Burning them in 
the span of decades injects that carbon into the fast 
cycle far quicker than photosynthesis, ocean uptake, 
and rock weathering can remove it again.

S E S S I O N R E C A P
The Four Mechanisms, Connected
1
Five Spheres
Earth's climate system is atmosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, lithosphere, and 
biosphere in constant interaction.
2
Energy Balance
Incoming solar energy (~100 units) versus outgoing heat (~70 absorbed/re-emitted, ~30 
reflected) sets the planet's temperature.
3
A Necessary Effect
The greenhouse effect keeps Earth ~33°C warmer than it would otherwise be —
essential, not inherently harmful.
4
Human Amplification
CO₂, methane, N₂O, and F-gases have intensified this natural process well past historical 
equilibrium.
5
Measured Warming
+1.1°C since pre-industrial times, accelerating sharply since 1980 — not a projection, a 
measurement.
6
Feedback Loops
Ice-albedo and permafrost carbon feedbacks can self-reinforce warming — the same 
nonlinear dynamics you study in systems.
7
Fast vs. Slow Carbon
Nature separates carbon into fast (days–centuries) and slow (millennia+) cycles — and 
fossil fuels bridge the two dangerously.
8
Human Disruption
Fossil combustion and deforestation moved carbon from the slow cycle into the fast 
cycle faster than sinks can absorb it.
9
A Ledger Problem
The global carbon budget is a resource-accounting system currently running a structural 
deficit.
10 Your Toolkit Applies
Systems thinking, feedback loops, and data modeling — skills you already have — are 
exactly what this problem needs.

S E C T I O N 1 · W H A T T H E W O R L D I S W A T C H I N G
Key Global Concerns
Climate change is not one problem — it is a cluster of interconnected, planet-wide risks.
Sea Level Rise
Melting ice sheets and thermal expansion 
threaten coastal cities and small island 
nations.
Extreme Weather
More frequent and intense heatwaves, 
floods, droughts, and storms.
Biodiversity Loss
Shifting habitats and temperatures push 
species toward extinction faster than they 
can adapt.
Food & Water Security
Changing rainfall and heat stress threaten 
crop yields and freshwater availability.
Climate Migration
Millions may be displaced by sea level rise, 
drought, and resource conflict in coming 
decades.
Public Health
Heat stress, disease vector spread, and air 
quality decline all worsen with warming.
Air Quality
Many drivers of climate change also directly 
worsen air pollution and respiratory illness.
Wildfires
Hotter, drier conditions extend fire seasons 
and increase their frequency and intensity.

S E C T I O N 1 · Y O U R A N G L E
Every Global Concern Is Also a Data Problem
Before any of these risks can be managed, they first have to be measured, modeled, and monitored — at planetary scale.
Early Warning Systems Flood, heatwave, and cyclone early-warning systems are fundamentally real-time data pipelines — sensors, 
models, and alerts racing against time.
Satellite Monitoring Deforestation, glacier retreat, and drought are tracked largely through satellite imagery pipelines processed with 
computer vision and ML.
Migration & Risk Modeling Predicting climate-driven displacement requires modeling human behavior against environmental data — a 
hard, unsolved computational problem.
The Opportunity Every concern on the previous slide has an unfilled software and data engineering gap behind it.
